Hong Kong Cable & Satellite Workers Walk Out, Disrupting Operations Across Sector

A coordinated walkout by cable and satellite workers has brought significant disruption to Hong Kong’s broadcasting and pay-TV sector, with ongoing impacts on content delivery, customer service, and technical maintenance. The strike, which began on Monday, involves employees from several leading industry players, including Eastern View Networks and Pearl Satellite Holdings, and is now entering its third day.

According to the Hong Kong Cable & Satellite Workers’ Union, approximately 1,200 technicians, engineers, and call-center staff have ceased work, citing unresolved disputes over wages, shift scheduling, and job security amid increasing automation. “We have not seen genuine engagement from management despite months of negotiation,” said union spokesperson Kelvin Chan at a press conference Tuesday. “Our members provide essential services that keep households connected and informed. We deserve fair terms.”

The walkout has led to mounting delays in installation and repair appointments, and many subscribers have reported interrupted access to both scheduled and on-demand programming. Several customer support hotlines operated by major providers are now unavailable or severely backlogged, with Pearl Satellite Holdings confirming an average wait time of two hours for technical assistance.

Industry analysts say the impact may deepen if the strike continues. “If this action extends into next week, we expect a substantial backlog in service requests and prolonged outages,” noted Lydia Wong, a sector analyst at Asia Broadcast Insights.

Management at Eastern View Networks issued a statement expressing hope for a swift resolution and urging staff to return to work, but as of Wednesday evening, talks remain at an impasse. The industry is bracing for ongoing disruption as negotiations continue.
